description: Every stakeholder original in the case-originals registry (examples/case_originals.json, plx-case-originals/v1, generated from two immutable source-pin records: the baseline c7a7ce0b context/8e511521...json (record sha256 5cfdad98...0cbe71, 81 inventory entries) and the incremental 024655de context/470a5d60...json (sha256 a20ba739...2e96, 11 pins, case register of 9 cases, 12 historical mail pins, 15 open gaps), plus four capture records of the Artwork_Missing_Evidence_part1-4.zip archives bound to the artwork lifecycle case (b45848e1 context/5ed665d0...json, 4d5159b6 context/6e920cf5...json, 5a2c543b context/fcc0f936...json, bfb07c40 context/46b6c69a...json; provider size and quickXorHash only), and the artwork originals manifest bound to the same case (78640266 context/1ce04e07...json, sha256 f2cd062d...1276: 15 source files, 18 attachments nested in their .msg parents and 8 members of the one nested zip; parents linked, a repeated payload aliased to its first row and counted once; no URL, body or secret kept): 92 file records, the Asset Tracker's 195.0 revision and the 12 historical mail pins as unfetched rows, the 4 capture rows and the 41 manifest rows = 150 entries, 17 open gaps) read in full by python3 -m scripts.case_originals read through the GET-only Graph clients only: a row with a drive item through SharePointReader.get_content (graph.drive_item then graph.drive_item_content and its 302, fetched credential-free on the tenant hosts), a manifest source row (drive id, path, list item unique id; no URL) through its parent folder's one listing (graph.drive_path then graph.drive_children, the exact name, its eTag GUID compared with the list item unique id; not listed gone path_not_located, two same-name files unavailable path_ambiguous, an unparseable eTag unavailable etag_unrecognised, another item there gone path_holds_other_item) and then graph.drive_item_content, a row with only a sharing/OneDrive URL through integrations.shared_link.read_shared_link (graph.share_drive_item), the Asset Tracker's historical 195.0 revision through SharePointReader.get_version_content (graph.drive_item_version_content and its 302; the pin names its size only, so it matches by bytes), the historical mail pins in the mailbox PLX_EVAL_EXPOSED_MAILBOX names through GraphMailReader (each message located by its exact received second in one oldest-first listing, then its text body read, stored and extracted, match_basis received_at; each pinned attachment found under it by name and verified by size and SHA-256; with no mailbox configured they read no_route mailbox_not_configured), the one derivative held in this repository's history (repository_ref, a GitHub blob URL at a commit) from the local Git object store only (git cat-file, no fetch). Each file's bytes are compared with the registry (size and SHA-256; a capture: size and the provider quickXorHash), its type detected from the bytes, and it is extracted by operating.use_case_parts; archive members and mail attachments are verified through their container's one read. A capture archive over use_case_intake.MAX_CONTENT_BYTES (parts 1-3: 100.3, 163.7 and 186.1 MB over 100 MB) is an oversize registry row and reads capped exceeds_cap (one metadata GET, no download); one under it is read in full and its receipt carries its SHA-256 and member manifest (path, name, bytes, SHA-256, type by bytes; a member over MAX_PART_BYTES oversize with its bound, counted). Rows proven by an earlier recorded capture are verified by hash only. A pinned file whose current bytes differ reads mismatch (the pinned row is kept) and the served bytes are their own revision receipt (rv-, revision_of the row, stored and extracted). Capture store: PLX_WORKBENCH_STATE_DIR (the runner's store), never Git: bytes at <state>/case-originals/<sha256>, text at <state>/case-originals/extractions/<sha256>.txt, one receipt per entry at <state>/case-originals/receipts/<registry sha256>/<entry id>.json (registry version, entry, name, watch folder, canonical source, provider revision and eTag read, bytes, sha256, match and its basis, body status, HTTP status and Graph error code, extraction status and method, member manifest, read time, reader identity). Watch folders (Vince's and Stephen's Teams Chat Files and Ricardo's process-maps folder through graph.share_drive_item, PLXSite's 'Artwork Lifecycle Examples' and AGENTS' 'Ontology UseCases' by drive id and path through graph.drive_path; children through graph.drive_children, recursively): every listed file the registry does not pin is read in full like an original (discovered_read with bytes, sha256, eTag, type by bytes and extraction), an item with no file facet is discovered_not_file, and a 403/404 names its HTTP status and Graph error code (404: gone). Output: counts by status, read_via (files read per route: drive_item, drive_path, drive_item_version, mail, shared_link, container, repository; the floor is one drive item read through Graph, so the local Git read alone never passes), failure_causes (one enum token per distinct status:http:code:detail:extraction), problem_pages (entry id -> that token for every entry not read or not matching, pages of 50), captures (per capture row: status, bytes, match, member counts), and on stdout only entry_pages (per entry: status, registered, name, watch folder, case, kind, source, sha256 match, HTTP status, error code, detail, extraction status, revision), the reader identity. Never a body, extracted text or URL; the recorded detail holds ids, enums and counts only. Read-only: GET only, token POST only. Findings audit (A1, A4; DOC-05, DOC-09): every read original with extracted text is rendered as the case finding it would become (operating.cases labels: cited_fact only when its citation, the stored bytes re-hashed with the stored text, resolves and the bytes matched, else model_output_interpretation) and every OCR-derived value (method tesseract-ocr) as a machine-read lead; the report carries counts only, case_findings {rendered, cited_fact, model_output_interpretation, mislabelled} and ocr_values {derived, machine_read_lead, verified_ocr}, and passes only with mislabelled 0, verified_ocr 0 and at least one finding rendered. ING-10: item_isolation reads the per-item outcomes; a failing item must be typed (untyped 0) and must not stop the run (stalled 0, later_read counts later items read); outcome not_exercised when no item failed, which is not a pass.
notes: Live-unverified until the live check records a result; injected-transport tested (tests/test_case_originals.py: registry rows from trimmed copies of both records, capture rows (oversize over a patched MAX_CONTENT_BYTES, unpinned pinned only from a verified full-read receipt with its member rows, an unknown capture input refused), PNG bytes named .pdf read as an image, a sha256 mismatch kept with its served revision as an rv- receipt, Graph 403 -> denied access_denied and 404 -> gone item_not_found, the historical revision read through its version content (matched by bytes; other bytes a bytes_mismatch), mail pins located by received second with the attachment verified, not located (gone message_not_located) or ambiguous (unavailable message_ambiguous) with the attachment sharing the reason, a located message's text body stored and extracted, a malformed pin unavailable invalid_pin (never a crash), no mailbox -> no_route mailbox_not_configured, the repository derivative read from a local Git object (the record's text field whose bytes carry the registered SHA-256), members and an EML attachment through one archive read, manifest sections to rows with parents, aliases and one payload count, an unknown or malformed manifest section refused, manifest sources read by drive path with their nested attachments and zip members through their container, one folder listing and one read each at 1/10/60 manifest rows, watch folders by sharing link and by drive id + path with every discovered file read in full (discovered_read), a package item discovered_not_file, a discovered 404 gone, 60 discovered files read once each, 60+ entries over 50-entry pages, identity fields, no body/text/secret/URL in stdout or the recorded detail). Body statuses: read, partial, capped (exceeds_cap), mismatch (sha256_mismatch or quick_xor_hash_mismatch; current_revision names the rv- receipt), denied (401/403, not_visible, read_only_guard), gone (404: item or link no longer exists), unavailable (other Graph failure, repository_ref_invalid, repository_object_absent, repository_unreadable, no_graph_source, not_in_container, member_unreadable, container_<status>, budget_cut), no_route (mailbox_not_configured: a historical mail pin with PLX_EVAL_EXPOSED_MAILBOX unset), gone also message_not_located / attachment_not_located, unavailable also message_ambiguous / attachment_ambiguous / invalid_pin, capped also a mail body past MAIL_BODY_CHARS, not_file (no_file_facet); discovered_* and revision_read for the receipts that are not registry rows. The check passes when every one of the 150 entries has a receipt, every entry not read names why, all 4 captures report and at least one file was read; a denied, gone, capped or mismatch entry is a recorded finding, not a failure. Unverified live: that the manifest's drive paths and eTag GUIDs still locate its 15 files and that its .msg parents yield the 18 attachments by name, that the app-only token resolves the owners' personal OneDrive Teams Chat Files links through /shares/ (an app-only 404 there is reported gone, which may also mean not shared with the app), that the runner's checkout holds commit e059ffc4 for the repository derivative (else repository_object_absent), that the Asset Tracker's current revision is still 197.0, part4's real member manifest (parts 1-3 stay oversize until the reader's content bound or a streaming archive read changes: docs/decisions/2026-10-17-artwork-oversize-archives.md). The registry pins part4's SHA-256 and manifest only by regenerating it with --pin-receipts over this check's receipts. Time: a forecast, not measured: the previous run of 105 entries finished inside 900 s; discovered files are now downloaded and extracted too and part4 adds 48 MB with its members, so --budget-seconds is 1800 and the timeout 2100 (the reader lists every watch folder first, and discovered files the budget leaves are a continuation, below); a slow estate reports budget_cut true (ok false, exit 1) only when a registry entry, a watch-folder listing or a registry file's OCR was cut, those entries unavailable budget_cut and counted, never a timeout kill. Discovered watch-folder files are listed first and read least recently read first; those the budget left are discovered_pending (unavailable budget_cut, their stored earlier read kept), a continuation that does not set budget_cut: the check passes while discovered_pending > 0 only when this run read at least one new discovered file (discovered_reused counts those an earlier run read, unchanged), and fails when files are pending and none was read, so a store that does not persist between runs and a folder larger than one budget still shows progress or fails. Oversize archive parts stay registry entries, so a cut on them still fails. gaps is a ceiling (json_max 17, the registry's diagnosed open gaps): a gap closed is an improvement, never a failure; undiagnosed stays 0 (A4). The reader's identity fields are recorded under reader, not asserted: each is null when its optional variable is unset, and a null asserted field fails.
